what_i_did: build.py is models/goat/build.py reshaped: the same 26 named parts plus two cheek plates, the same hierarchy and pivots (body > neck > head > nose/eyes/horns/ears > ear insides/beard; body > tail; body > leg upper > lower > hoof), the same POSE table and the same materials (Fur_Cream, Fur_Tan, Horn_Tan, Horn_Hoof, Skin_Pink, Skin_Eye) plus one new one, Skin_Blush, for the rosy cheeks. Z up, origin at the footprint centre on the ground, head to -Y.
The normal goat's shape numbers were sheet pixels; the charming sheet is dropped, so the numbers in P are plain metres as (y, z) side-view points.

Only the hero is scored. The turnaround sheet draws a leggy kid with a long upright neck in the front and back views, and its middle view is a three-quarter view with the face turned to the camera, not a side elevation; the hero (a big round head right on a round fluffy body, short stubby legs) wins, so all three sheet views are dropped. make_views.py keys the hero again: the harness mask lost most of the cream fur against the cream backdrop and kept the warm cast shadow, which is as saturated as the tan hooves. The key uses a saturation test against the per-row backdrop, cuts everything below the belly except hand-measured leg boxes, and paints pixels the harness shadow test would drop tan, so harness.target_mask() recovers exactly the cleaned silhouette.

hero_check.py renders the model from the hero's own direction (the goat's left side, 40 deg round towards the front, 3 deg up, from a yaw/elevation grid search) with the harness lens and scores its silhouette against views/hero.png. The standard harness front/side/back renders are in r/ for reference but have no target.

idle: standing, head up, cocked and turned as in the hero. feeding: a chibi with a short neck cannot reach the grass standing, so it kneels as real goats do: the front cannons fold back (knees on the ground), the body pitches nose-down about the hind hooves (solved by bisection, 9 deg), then the neck swings down until the muzzle is 3 cm off the ground with the face pitch held at 80 deg (neck 107 deg); ears droop, tail down. rest: front and hind legs fold under, the body drops until the belly is 4 cm off the ground, head up.

python tools/ranch-rebuild/to_game.py goat-charming wrote simulation-assets-charming/organics/goat-{idle,feeding,rest}.{json,glb} (and the sandbox2-runtime mirror). The nose is at +X as in the normal goat-idle.json and every material maps to the skin role.
good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.775 (768 px, 48 samples): the big round head with its cock and turn, the chunky back-curling horns, the floppy ears, the round shaggy barrel, the pom-pom tail and the stubby legs in tan socks.
2954 triangles in every pose, under the 3k goat budget.
Reads as the same goat as the normal one (same colours, horns, beard, tan legs, upright tail), only as a plush toy.
off: Footprint is wider than the normal goat: 0.60 x 1.12 m (width/length 0.54) against 0.45 x 0.98 (0.46). The big head and the floppy ears the hero needs set the width; in the game, scaled to the normal length, the charming goat is about 20 % wider and 12 % lower than the normal one.
The ears hang more steeply than the hero's (narrowed to hold the footprint), so they read as slimmer flaps from the side and the hero overlay misses some ear area.
The hero's fine fur strokes are modelled as large hanging locks round the belly and a few puffs on the back and legs; finer fur would not read at tile size.
The game's flat normals make the plush toy look faceted rather than smooth; the forms are kept round with more segments and little jitter.
In the feeding pose the head turn (baked into the head) makes the face graze slightly sideways.

rounds.change: First charming build from the normal goat's skeleton: round barrel, big round head with a short muzzle on a hidden stub neck, chunky horns, floppy ears, stubby legs, upright pom-pom tail, rosy cheeks, belly puffs, head cocked 9 deg and turned 14 deg. Hero view grid-searched (yaw 35, elev 4).
Head 20 % bigger and further forward, horns and ears moved with it, eyes and cheeks placed on the head surface, chunkier legs and hooves.
Eyes protrude so they show, ears hung steeper and the head turn cut to 10 deg to bring the width back towards the normal footprint (0.64 to 0.56 m).
Body, hind legs and tail moved back (longer barrel, as in the hero; footprint ratio 0.50). Same view 0.753; the view search moved to yaw 40, elev 3, where it scores 0.766.
Head another 8 % bigger, horns raised, ears further out and higher (the hero's ears dominate its silhouette).
Belly puffs turned into overlapping hanging locks (a shaggy skirt instead of a bead string), broader ears, leg cuffs trimmed to stay under budget. Final render at 768 px, 48 samples: 0.775.

moving_parts: No animation (the game poses the model). Every part is pivoted at its joint as in the normal goat, so the poses are joint rotations from the POSE table, plus a solved body pitch for kneeling and a body drop for rest.
creative_additions: Rosy cheek plates (new Skin_Blush material), a forelock puff between the horns, a fluffy crest along the back, fur cuffs at the knees, a beard with two soft locks, and the kneeling graze for feeding.
changes_from_normal: Head about 2.5 x the normal volume, round, carried on the chest with no visible neck, cocked 9 deg and turned 10 deg towards the viewer; short rounded muzzle; big eyes and blush cheeks; chunky curled horns; long floppy ears instead of the sideways leaf ears; a round barrel body with a shaggy skirt of hanging locks instead of the slim faceted body with shards; legs half as long and much thicker with tan socks and big rounded hooves; a pom-pom tail; feeding kneels; lower jitter for a soft moulded look.
